Evaluate ${\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=(y-x)\,i-x\,j$ and $C$ is the arc of the ellipse ${x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}=2$  traversed counterclockwise from the point $(\sqrt{2},0)$ to the point $(0,1).$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Notice that we can write its equation as

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}=1.
$$

So, our curve is a part-ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal and vertical semiaxes $\sqrt{2}$ and $1$ respectively. This curve can be parameterized as

$$
r(t)=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,0\le t\le \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

So, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(y-x)\,i-x\,j \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =((\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot (-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\sqrt{2}({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡2t-\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t-\sqrt{2}\,dt \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t-\sqrt{2}t]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\frac{\pi \sqrt{2}}{2}]-[-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-0] \\  & =[\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\pi \sqrt{2}}{2}]-[-\frac{1}{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\pi \sqrt{2}}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =1-\frac{\pi \sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
